small_guidance:
- The conv (Conv3d on 128×3×16×32×32 → 16 out, k=3) almost certainly dominates the 0.86 ms; the fused tail kernel is already efficient. Add a `triton.autotune` over `(BLOCK_S ∈ {128,256,512}, BLOCK_C=16, num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3,4})` on `_fused_norm_clamp_max_kernel` to squeeze the tail, but expect <5% gain.
- Since C=16 fits exactly in BLOCK_C, drop the `for c_start in range(0,C,BLOCK_C)` loop and the `tl.where(c_mask, …, -inf)` — load a single [16,BLOCK_S] tile, fuse stats + clamp + max in one persistent pass per (n) so the data never touches HBM twice. This removes the separate `_stats_kernel` launch entirely.
- For the stats kernel, BLOCK_S=1024 with S=14×30×30=12600 means 13 iterations; bump to BLOCK_S=2048 and num_warps=8 to halve loop overhead.
large_guidance:
- The conv dominates — write a custom Conv3d Triton kernel (im2col-style GEMM, one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile), K = IC·kd·kh·kw = 81) and fuse the multiplier into the epilogue. This is the high-headroom move; the existing post-conv fusion already runs near memory-bound.
- Make the conv kernel emit `[N, C, S]` in channels-last (NDHWC) layout so the downstream norm+clamp+max kernel can load the channel dim contiguously and reduce across C with a single vector op (C=16 fits one warp).
- Collapse stats + normalize + clamp + ×mult + channel-max into a single persistent kernel per (N) that keeps the [16, S] tile resident in registers/shared memory: one pass to compute per-channel mean/var (Welford or two-pass over S-tiles), then a second pass over the same tile producing the channel-reduced output. Eliminates the mean/invstd HBM round-trip.
